biology: Collected inside a decayed trunk lying on the ground.
soldier: Very small in size; the appearance resembles that of Pseudocapritermes pseudolaetus, but the frontal ridge is not projecting. The head is reddish yellow, the mandibles brown, the antennae and the thorax and abdomen pale yellow, and the whole body is covered with short hairs. The head is long and tubular, the sides parallel; the dorsal longitudinal suture extends from the posterior margin to half the length of the head. The anterior one-fifth of the dorsum of the head slopes forwards as a facet, the crest of the slope being sinuous and blunt in lateral view, not forming a ridge-like projection. The fontanelle lies on the upper part of the slope. The labrum is narrow and strip-like, longer than wide, its anterior margin concave, both the left and the right corner needle-like. The postmentum is widest at its very front end and narrows slightly posteriorly, narrowest at the posterior third. The right mandible is shorter and slightly sinuous, its anterior end sharp; the left mandible is longer with considerable sinuation, with a swollen part near the anterior end, beyond which it gradually narrows and bends into a hook whose tip points antero-dextrally. Antennae with 14 segments, segments 3 and 4 about equal in length, segment 2 slightly longer. The anterior half of the pronotum rises vertically, shaped like a low, flat semicircle, the middle of the anterior margin slightly sinuous, the notch not distinct. The abdomen is slender and long.
